item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=empirical+case+studies+computational+creativity+autonomous+problem+formulation&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1201/b11471-9\", \"title\": [\"Problem Formulation and MCDA Model\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1201/b11471-9\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2011, 10, 24]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.2943891\", \"title\": [\"Empirical Choice Model Formulation for Metro Rail Location Problem\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>In this paper we let commuter’s utility function to include variables denoting the travel time to the metro location and quality of the metro service. Both variables are deﬁned as the function of a location’s utilization. Therefore, it leads to mixed integer non-linear model formulation as done in empirical choice models. It is assumed that the travel time to the location can be considered categorical, i.e. the variable takes on only few discrete values.
